lyrics:
[Intro: staccato orchestral string stabs, handclaps, deep bass]
Go on, go on, it's your half birthday
Six months in and it's your day anyway
We don't need a reason, we don't need a date
Pull a candle out the drawer, let's celebrate

[Verse 1: laid-back male rap, melodic drawl]
I got a cake in the car and it's leaning to the left
Frosting on the seat belt, nothing I regret
Stopped for balloons and they only had two
One says "Get Well" and the other one's blue
Called up your people and they're coming in their slippers
Your neighbour brought a casserole, your uncle brought the kippers
No one knows the reason and nobody's keeping score
We're just glad you made it halfway, so we're knocking on the door

[Chorus: sung drawl, claps on every beat]
Go on, go on, it's your half birthday
Six months in and it's your day anyway
We don't need a reason, we don't need a date
Pull a candle out the drawer, let's celebrate

[Verse 2: laid-back male rap, a little quieter]
See, a year's too long to wait to say you're doing fine
I've lost a couple friends who thought they had the time
So I'm ringing every bell on every ordinary Tuesday
If you woke up this morning then it's good news day
Half a glass, half a chance, half a life to go
Half of what we worry on, we'll never even know
So blow out the one candle, make half a wish
And I'll be back in six months with another dish

[Chorus: sung drawl, claps on every beat]
Go on, go on, it's your half birthday
Six months in and it's your day anyway
We don't need a reason, we don't need a date
Pull a candle out the drawer, let's celebrate

[Bridge: strings drop out, bass and claps, crowd sings along]
Halfway there (halfway there)
And you're still right here (still right here)
Halfway there (halfway there)
See you next half year

[Final Chorus: full beat, crowd, ad-libs]
Go on, go on, it's your half birthday
Six months in and it's your day anyway
We don't need a reason, we don't need a date
Pull a candle out the drawer, let's celebrate

[Outro: stabs and claps, a party horn, laughter]
Make a wish
Half a wish
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 90 BPM, 4/4, C-sharp minor. A slow, heavy bounce with a lot of space in it. Relaxed and grinning.

VOICE: Male baritone, laid-back and slightly slurred, sliding between rapping and a sing-song drawl. He never raises his voice. A crowd of friends answers in the bridge and joins the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: Short, staccato orchestral string stabs that form the riff. Handclaps on every backbeat. A deep, simple 808-style bass. A sparse kick and snare. A high synth whistle line in the chorus. A thin guitar pluck doubling the stabs. A party horn and room laughter at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the stabs and claps, and the hook straight away. 0:21 Verse 1, eight lines. 0:43 Chorus 1. 1:04 Verse 2, slightly quieter, the reason for the song. 1:26 Chorus 2. 1:47 Bridge, the strings drop out and the crowd sings back. 2:08 Final chorus with ad-libs. 2:30 The beat rides with the whistle line. 3:00 Outro, stabs and claps, a party horn, two spoken lines at 3:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s club rap: very clean, very sparse, sub-heavy, with the voice dry and in the middle and every clap sharp.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first line, sung over nothing but stabs and claps.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The swagger is replaced with affection, and verse 2 gives the reason: the singer has lost friends who thought there was time. Being halfway is something to mark.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Mischief, a serious beat, then generosity.
